flags.note: L2-CITATION-DIVERGENCE: pay_or_quit nonpayment notice — divergence detected. GPT (gpt-5.5): 3d | Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-13(3). Gemini (gemini-2.5-pro): 3d | Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-13(3). Human review required.  ATTORNEY NOTE: Confirmed: §89-8-13(5)(a), 3-day notice for nonpayment.

gpt_answer.rationale: For residential tenancies, if rent is unpaid when due, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement only if the tenant fails to pay within three days after written notice of nonpayment and the landlord’s intent to terminate. This establishes a three-day notice period for nonpayment before proceeding based on termination.

gemini_answer.rationale: The landlord must give the tenant three days' written notice of nonpayment and the intention to terminate the rental agreement. If the tenant does not pay the rent due within that period, the landlord may then terminate the agreement and begin eviction proceedings.

resolution.note: L2-AI-RESOLVED: Citation corrected from Miss. Code Ann. §89-7-27 to Miss. Code Ann. §89-8-13(5)(a). §89-8-13(5)(a) (Residential Landlord and Tenant Act) is the operative nonpayment provision: if the material noncompliance by the tenant is the nonpayment of rent, the landlord may deliver notice specifying the rental agreement will terminate if payment is not made within three (3) days. Verified from law.justia.com. §89-7-27 is from Chapter 7 (general/commercial); §89-8-13(5)(a) (Chapter 8) is the residential-specific nonpayment provision. Both GPT and Gemini cited §89-8-13; correct subsection for nonpayment is (5)(a). Period (3d) confirmed correct. Pending human confirmation.

elements: Tenant engaged in protected activity (habitability complaint, union organizing, exercising legal rights)
Landlord knew of the protected activity
Adverse action (eviction, rent increase, service reduction) followed protected activity
Causal connection between protected activity and adverse action
Action was within state-defined presumption period (varies: 60 days to 12 months)
substantive_defenses.note: Anti-retaliation statute: Miss. Code Ann. §89-8-17. Presumption period, protected activities, and available remedies vary by state — attorney verification required. Statute identified via machine-assisted retrieval — attorney verification required before use

elements: Tenant is member of a protected class (race, color, national origin, sex, disability, familial status, religion — per federal FHA; state law may add classes)
Similarly situated non-protected tenants were treated more favorably, OR discriminatory intent can be shown, OR facially neutral policy has disparate impact
substantive_defenses.statute: 42 U.S.C. §3604 (Fair Housing Act); Miss. Code Ann. §43-33-13
substantive_defenses.note: Federal FHA prohibits discrimination in housing based on protected class. State law may provide additional protected classes and remedies. Discriminatory intent or disparate impact analysis is fact-intensive — specialist review required. grounding_gap: state fair housing case law and protected class details.

elements: Tenant had a valid lease or tenancy
Landlord substantially interfered with tenant's right to peaceful possession
substantive_defenses.note: Breach of covenant of quiet enjoyment — primarily common law doctrine in most states; some states codify at RLTA. grounding_gap: whether state recognizes as affirmative defense to eviction, constructive eviction standard, and remedies vary — specialist review required.

elements: Amount demanded in notice exceeds lawfully owed rent
Impermissible charges included (late fees, utilities, damages, other non-rent items)
substantive_defenses.note: Improper rent calculation — relevant where landlord has included improper charges (late fees, fees not authorized by lease) in the rent demand. grounding_gap: state-specific rules on what may be included in rent demand, and whether overcharge voids notice — specialist review required.
